requests.request: A current-record view of a static index, or World.journaled_entities(): the entity ids journaled by mut / create / destroy in the current step, without the quiet temperature-only ones. With it a system can visit static_index(predicate reading a dynamic field) | journaled ids, filtered by the current record, exactly. Use: cleaning.drying scans the 5 drying fields of every entity once per 120 s (70-75 us per run on seed 1's 871 entities, ~0.023 ms per substep in bench_systems) and cleaning.soak filters ~176 holders for litres each substep (8 us). journal_keys() is not a substitute: at drying's substeps of the bench it holds ~800 entities (kernel thermal's set_quiet writes; repro: scratch p1f_cleaning/journal_bench.py).

Cheaper static-index builds when the caller declares reads=(...): evaluate the plain record for entities with no journal or quiet entry even mid-step (their _start_view is the record itself) and a view only for journaled ones. Since the read views (review M3) cleaning's eight first lookups cost 0.14-0.37 ms each on an 871-entity house (repro: scratch p1f_cleaning/index_build.py: liners 0.37, wet_floor_signs 0.36, liquid_holders 0.33, waste_containers 0.29, food_scraps / spills / debris / appliances ~0.2), ~0.042 ms per substep of the 40-substep bench vs 0.024 at ADOPT; cleaning would then declare its predicates' reads.

plumbing_liquids.details (order 120) gives vessel_feel and a touch grant on temperature_c on a close look only to vessels holding litres (L.holds_liquid / liquid_container), and grants the touch without asking the grant gate (out of reach it raises in strict mode).
